classification.difficultyReason: Identify the common rectangle height from the quadrant radii, then add the rectangle and two quadrant areas.

content.prompt: A hockey goal ‘circle’ is made up of a rectangle and two quadrants, as shown below. Find its approximate area, using $\pi\approx3.14$.

spec.description: Two quadrants flank a central rectangle. The baseline segments are labelled 20 m, 4 m and 20 m. Red internal vertical boundaries distinguish the components. The rectangle has a short horizontal top joining the quadrant arcs. Ordinary outlines and labels use house black; meaningful component boundaries use house red.
spec.mathematics: Each quadrant has radius 20 m. The central rectangle has width 4 m and height 20 m. The two quadrants together have half the area of a circle of radius 20 m.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied component boundaries and baseline measurements are visible.

answer.short:
$708\ \mathrm{m}^2$

Add the rectangle’s area to the areas of the two quadrants.
answer.worked:
The rectangle’s height equals the quadrant radius, $20\ \mathrm{m}$.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{rectangle}}&=4\times20\\A_{\text{rectangle}}&=80\ \mathrm{m}^2\\A_{\text{two quadrants}}&=2\times\frac14\times\pi\times20^2\\A_{\text{two quadrants}}&=200\pi\ \mathrm{m}^2\\A_{\text{total}}&=80+200\pi\\A_{\text{total}}&\approx80+200\times3.14\\A_{\text{total}}&\approx708\ \mathrm{m}^2\end{align*}$$
